RGenEDA: Genomic Exploratory Data Analysis

Source: R/RGenEDA-package.R
RGenEDA-package.Rd

RGenEDA collects the plots and summaries that are repeated in most bulk RNA-seq exploratory data analyses (EDA), built around the DESeq2 workflow, into one S4 object, geneda, and a set of functions that work on it.

Typical workflow

  1. Build a geneda object with GenEDA() (from matrices) or as.geneda() (from a SummarizedExperiment, DESeqDataSet or DESeqTransform).

  2. Check the data with PlotCountDist(), PlotDistances() and PlotHVGVariance().

  3. Select highly variable genes with FindVariableFeatures() and run PCA with RunPCA(). Explore it with PlotScree(), PlotPCA(), extractEigen(), PlotEigenHeatmap() and PlotEigenCorr(); use PlotOrdCorr() for NMDS ordination instead of PCA.

  4. Store differential expression results with SetDEGs(), filter them with FilterDEGs() and FindHVDEGs(), and plot them with PlotMA(), PlotVolcano(), PlotPValHist() or DEDashboard().

  5. Save heatmaps with GenSave().

Data are read with the accessors getCounts(), getNormalized(), getMetadata(), HVGs(), DimReduction() and DEGs(). The example dataset is Snail1KO. See vignette("Snail1_Vignette", package = "RGenEDA") for a full walk-through.
